channel.description: Approved local stories in broadcast order

item.description: A coastal storm brought freezing rain and strong winds to Vermont and northern New York last night. Wind gusts reached up to sixty miles per hour in Rutland and Bennington counties. Power outages and hazardous travel conditions were reported. Green Mountain Power Vermont Electric Cooperative and Washington Electric Co-op report two thousand six hundred seventy nine still without power in Vermont this morning.

The Regional Food Bank gave out over five hundred seventy thousand meals across New York this Thanksgiving. In the North Country, about ten thousand meals were distributed at several locations including Plattsburgh and Ticonderoga. Volunteers helped provide free Thanksgiving meals to thousands in need.

New York DEC awarded forty-five million dollars to support tree planting and forest markets. Adirondack projects received seven and a half million dollars, including five million to Lyme Adirondack Forest Company. Funding expands native tree nurseries and forest product markets.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul delayed Medicaid work requirements until June next year. The rules require recipients to show eighty hours a month of work or education, with some exemptions. The state is upgrading systems and hopes for federal changes to ease these rules.
